/projects/3d-reconstruction: My MEng group project: a 3D reconstruction framework built with industrial use in mind, such as VR simulation, live room tracking and medical imaging.
/projects/ai-decision-trees: Machine learning coursework in which I built decision tree models in Python for a cybersecurity problem, detecting financial fraud. It covered processing the data as well as tuning the models.
/projects/ai-search-algorithms: AI coursework where we implemented search algorithms, measured how they performed on hard problems, and designed our own heuristics to speed them up.
/projects/autonomous-robotics: A ROS2 project where a simulated TurtleBot3 explores a space on its own, finds colored objects with computer vision and drives up to them precisely.
/projects/business-plan: A business plan for an AI tool that writes up NHS clinical documentation, so doctors spend less time on paperwork. The plan targets 1.8 million UK healthcare professionals and builds on £2 billion of government digitalization funding.
/projects/c-programming: A set of C programs for three custom image file formats, with compression schemes that work down at the bit level.
/projects/data-mining: A research proposal, written in the EPSRC format, for an AI system that drafts medical documentation within NHS workflows. It follows the CRISP-DM methodology from start to finish.
/projects/distributed-systems: A serverless, ERP-style inventory management workflow I built on Microsoft Azure Functions. It puts cloud computing, Function-as-a-Service architecture and distributed system design into practice.
/projects/formula-student-ai: I joined the simulation team of Leeds University's autonomous racing team, which builds a self-driving car for the international Formula Student AI competition. The simulation team built the environments used to test the car's autonomous subsystems.
/projects/graphics-fundamentals: Computer Graphics Coursework 1. I implemented the core 2D graphics algorithms in C++, including line drawing, triangle rasterization and image blitting, then tested and benchmarked them.
/projects/home-lab: My home lab is a desktop with an RTX 5090 that runs local LLMs and coding agents, plus a Raspberry Pi that stays on all the time. Tailscale links them to my laptop and phone, so I can use all of it from anywhere.
/projects/machine-learning: Machine learning coursework in which I implemented linear regression with custom basis functions, then used Principal Component Analysis to visualize 3D medical data.
/projects/medical-simulation: A research tool that simulates how a flow diverter stent deploys inside a patient's own blood vessel geometry.
/projects/mental-health-app: A software design brief for a £100,000 mental health app for university students around the world. The design centers on a ChatGPT-4 Turbo companion and covers the stakeholders, the system architecture, links into university systems, crisis intervention and privacy controls.
/projects/numerical-computation: Numerical analysis coursework where I implemented and compared differential equation solvers on a predator-prey model, then measured their error and running time.
/projects/opengl-renderer: Computer Graphics Coursework 2. A 3D renderer in modern OpenGL that implements the full projective graphics pipeline. It renders real terrain with lighting, and includes a space launch you can control.
/projects/parallel-computing: Three pieces of coursework in OpenMP, MPI and OpenCL, covering shared memory, distributed message passing and GPU programming.
/projects/pnanolocz: The first phase of porting NanoLocz, a MATLAB application for AFM (Atomic Force Microscopy) analysis, to Python.
/projects/portfolio: This is the site you're on. It started as a Blazor WebAssembly app on .NET 8, and I've rebuilt it as I learned. It's now server-rendered on .NET 10, with a 3D homepage, an AI assistant and an MCP server.
/projects/quantum-dots: A nanotechnology business case for investing in a company that manufactures quantum dots, the light sources behind quantum computing with light.
/projects/synergy: Hybrid C#/.NET and Python platform transforming codebases into queryable graphs with architectural intelligence, featuring ASP.NET Core API, Blazor WASM UI, and active "Architectural Linter" capabilities for AI-assisted development
/projects/terratracker: A full-stack app for recording and sharing GPS routes, built by a team of six working in agile sprints. We documented every sprint and ran the project through Git the way a professional team would.
/projects/xv6-operating-system: Operating systems coursework where I wrote a Unix-style shell for xv6 and extended its kernel with new system calls.
/vascular-blood-flow: For my dissertation I built a Lattice Boltzmann Method (LBM) framework that simulates pulsing blood flow through arteries. The aim was to move research-style simulation closer to something clinicians could use to assess aneurysm risk.
